{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./filt1.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   --nodes=1              -> -N 1
#   --ntasks=1             -> -n 1
#   --cpus-per-task=4      -> -c 4
#   --time=00:240:00       -> -t 240m  (Slurm syntax suggests 240 minutes)
#   --array=0-39           -> submit 40 jobs (best-effort via flux submit --cc)

# NOTE: Slurm -A phillipslab not translated.
# Performance/ops implication: accounting/charging may not be applied as intended; site may require account/project out-of-band.

# NOTE: Slurm --partition=phillips not translated.
# Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible resources; you are not forcing the phillips partition.

# NOTE: Slurm --job-name=filt1 not translated.
# Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance is unaffected.

# Submit 40 jobs; use task rank (0..39) to emulate SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID.
flux submit --cc=40 -N 1 -n 1 -c 4 -t 240m \
  bash -lc '
    set -e

    SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID=${FLUX_TASK_RANK:-0}
    export OMP_NUM_THREADS=4

    module load easybuild icc/2017.1.132-GCC-6.3.0-2.27 impi/2017.1.132 skewer

    cd /projects/phillipslab/ateterina/CR_popgen/data/reads/ || exit 1

    LISTFILES=(*.fastq)
    file=${LISTFILES[$SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID]}

    # remove adapter + qc
    skewer -x AGATCGGAAGAG -t 4 -q 20 -l 36 -d 0.1 -r 0.1 -o ${file/_1.fastq/.tr1} $file ${file/_1.fastq/_2.fastq}

    mv ${file/_1.fastq/.tr1-trimmed-pair1.fastq} ${file/_1.fastq/_fp1.ok.fastq}
    mv ${file/_1.fastq/.tr1-trimmed-pair2.fastq} ${file/_1.fastq/_fp2.ok.fastq}
  '
"
}
